description: NVMe SSD Device Health Metrics (Lifetime, Temperature, Read/Write Operation Count, Critical Warning)

panels.description: Read and write throughput as the Linux block layer accounts for it, from node-exporter. Compare with "Data Units Read and Written to Device" below, which is the drive's own accounting of the same traffic.
panels.title: NVMe Throughput

panels.description: Throughput as the drive itself accounts for it, from the SMART data-unit counters (1000 x 512-byte blocks each, hence x 512000). Compare with NVMe Throughput above, which is what the kernel block layer saw.
panels.title: Data Units Read and Written to Device

panels.description: Vendor estimate of endurance consumed, as a percentage of the drive's rated write endurance. It is allowed to exceed 100%; the drive does not stop working when it does.
panels.title: Percent Used

panels.description: Composite controller temperature reported in the SMART log.
panels.title: Temperature

panels.description: SMART critical-warning bit 4: the subsystem has degraded to the point of affecting reliability. Any value other than OK warrants attention.
panels.title: NVM Subsystem Reliability

panels.description: SMART critical-warning bit 1: the composite temperature is above the over-temperature threshold or below the under-temperature threshold.
panels.title: Temperature Threshold

panels.description: SMART critical-warning bit 0: available spare capacity has fallen below the threshold shown in "Spare Threshold".
panels.title: Available Spare

panels.description: Lifetime count of entries in the drive's error information log. Grows monotonically; a jump means something new went wrong.
panels.title: Error Log Entries

panels.description: Remaining spare blocks as a percentage of the factory allotment. Falling towards "Spare Threshold" means the drive is running out of replacements for worn blocks.
panels.title: Available Spare Capacity

panels.description: The level at which the drive raises the Available Spare critical warning. Compare against "Available Spare Capacity" above.
panels.title: Spare Threshold

panels.description: SMART critical-warning bit 3: the media has been placed in read-only mode. The drive will accept no further writes.
panels.title: Read Only

panels.description: SMART critical-warning bit 4: the volatile-memory backup device has failed. Only meaningful on drives that have one.
panels.title: Volatile Backup Failed

panels.description: SMART critical-warning bit 5: the Persistent Memory Region has become read-only or unreliable.
panels.title: Persistent Mem Read Only

panels.description: Lifetime count of unrecovered data-integrity errors: uncorrectable ECC, CRC failures, and LBA tag mismatches. Should stay at zero.
panels.title: Media Error

panels.description: Lifetime power-on count, plotted against the subset of those that ended in an unsafe shutdown (power lost before the drive was told to stop).
panels.title: Power Cycles

panels.description: Fraction of time the drive spends above its warning and critical composite-temperature thresholds. The counters are in minutes, so the rate is scaled by 60 to read as a duty cycle.
panels.title: Warning Temperature

panels.description: Cumulative hours the drive has been powered on over its lifetime.
panels.title: Power on Hours

panels.description: Total bytes read from and written to the device over its lifetime. SMART reports these as "data units" of 1000 x 512-byte blocks, so the raw counter is scaled by 512000 to get bytes.
panels.title: Data Read/Written (lifetime)

panels.description: Lifetime count of read and write commands the host has issued. Divided into the data-unit counters, this gives average command size.
panels.title: Host Command Read/Write

panels.description: Cumulative time the controller has spent servicing I/O. The SMART counter is in minutes and is scaled by 60 here so the unit reads as seconds.
panels.title: Controller Busy Time

list.description: The node which the metrics were collected from.
list.label: Node
list.name: Node

list.description: This is a variable for the NVMe device to be queried.
list.label: NVMe Device
list.name: device

list.description: This is a shorted version of the NVMe device with the /dev/ prefix removed.
list.label: NVMe Device (short)
list.name: device_short

title: NVMe Exporter Device Metrics
